item.title: News Wrap: Defense rests in murder trial of Lindsay Clancy
item.description:
On Friday, the defense rested in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, who has admitted to strangling her three young children to death. Closing arguments are expected early next week, after which the case will go to the jury. The 36-year-old former labor and delivery nurse is on trial for three counts of first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths of her children at the family’s home in Duxbury, Massachusetts. Clancy’s children were 5 years old, 3 years old, and 8 months old. She has pleaded not guilty. The case has become a lightning rod with the public, largely because Clancy’s defense argues that she had postpartum psychosis at the time of the killings. Clancy’s defense team is relying on what’s commonly referred to as the insanity defense to argue that she was not criminally responsible because of her mental state. item.title: Watch: Moment robot attempts to beat Usain Bolt's 100m record
item.description:
If you were worried about killer cyborgs taking over the world anytime soon, you can breathe a sigh of relief for the moment. Artificial intelligence may be getting smarter, but it turns out some supposedly high-tech robots still haven’t figured out what a kindergarten kid learns on a bicycle: how to hit the brakes. A high-speed demonstration at Beijing’s National Speed Skating Oval turned into an absolute comedy show when a state-of-the-art Chinese humanoid robot dashing around the track lost control and slammed headfirst into a barrier. The epic fail occurred during practice runs for the upcoming 2nd World Humanoid Robot Games. Unitree’s “H1” model was showing off its insane speed inside the famous “Ice Ribbon” stadium, tearing around the indoor track to prepare for the big event. item.title: Lindsay Clancy suffering 'command hallucination' when she killed children, court hears
item.description:
Another summer, another high-profile trial for everyone to lose their mind over. There was Boston’s Karen Read in 2024, Amber Heard and Johnny Depp’s battle over who abused who worse a few years before that, and now, there’s the case of Lindsay Clancy. Clancy, whose legal team says she was suffering from postpartum psychosis , strangled her three children to death in the basement of her Massachusetts home in early 2023, and neither she nor her lawyers deny that. The murder trial that’s taking place now is to ascertain whether Clancy should spend the rest of her life in prison, or in a mental institution. item.title: Prof. Musa Al-Gharbi's "Jason Arday and Me"
item.description:
A very interesting piece in the Chronicle of Higher Education . Here are two brief excerpts, but they can't do justice to the whole piece, which covers much more ground: {[W]hen a mainstream journalist [investigated Arday], he was threatened with lawsuits , visited by the police , and subsequently instructed by his editors to bury the story—and he sheepishly complied. Arday was exposed by a "race realist" Substack writer because reporters wouldn't cover the story until after it had already become common knowledge . It seems to defeat the purpose of the journalistic profession to tell people what they've already learned by other means, but that was the position U.K. media outlets and journalists took: radio silence until "others" started the conversation. And, somehow, the main lesson many seem to be taking from the way things played out is that we need even more media censorship…

item.title: Settlers target Palestinian homes in Occupied West Bank’s Area B
item.description:
Report says violence is moving from Israeli-controlled areas to those earmarked for a future Palestinian state Violent Israeli settler attacks in the two areas of the occupied West Bank under direct Palestinian rule have almost doubled since 2025, as settlers pursue a self-proclaimed “great settlement revolution” in the very heart of the territory earmarked for a Palestinian state. According to a report by the Israeli human rights organisation Yesh Din , shared with the Guardian, data shows that almost two-thirds of incidents of settler violence so far in 2026 have taken place in the so-called Areas A and B – placed under Palestinian Authority governance in the 1995 Oslo accords.
